transcript: Okay, so I just got back from seeing Betsy Wolfe's first performance in Death Becomes Her, and while I will post my full thoughts tomorrow, I did just want to quickly talk about the ad libs tonight, because if you don't know, death Becomes her has two main ad lib spots. The first is the wedding sponsor, and tonight's wedding was sponsored by Nina Simone. It's a new dawn, it's a new day, and I'm feeling good. Which is just a nod to how she was feeling about her first performance. But if there is a deeper significance to that, let me know. And then at the end of the show, we have another ad lib when Madeline asked Helen, what do you wanna do tomorrow? And tonight? Madeline said, let's go see Spelling Bee, to which Madeline replied, Sisyphean. And this is actually a nod to the fact that both Betsy and Jen played Rona Lisa Perez in the original production of Spelling Bee, in all of its iterations. I believe Betsy was San Francisco and Jen did it on Broadway as a replacement. And their character was a previous winner of the spelling bee, having won off the word Sisyphean, which is why they both shouted Sisyphean. So I thought that was really sweet, but all in all, it was a really special performance, and I was so glad that I could be there for her debut.
